Lead Abatement in Philadelphia, PA

Much of Philadelphia's housing predates the 1978 ban on lead paint, which makes old coatings a fair assumption until a test says otherwise. Whether you found peeling paint on a porch, received a rental certification notice or plan to remodel, start by describing what you see and we will point you to the right lead service.

What toxic lead abatement actually covers

Most people searching for lead abatement are really trying to answer a smaller question first: does my house have a lead problem, and what kind? The word covers a chain of separate services. A lead paint inspection finds lead paint. A risk assessment finds hazards. Abatement itself, meaning lead paint removal, replacement, enclosure or encapsulation, is the permanent fix, and clearance testing confirms the dust is gone afterward.

Philadelphia adds a local layer. The city's Lead Paint Disclosure and Certification Law requires owners of pre-1978 rentals to have the property certified lead-safe or lead-free by a dust wipe technician before signing a lease or holding a rental license. Rental owners should confirm the current rules with the city rather than rely on an old checklist.

Pennsylvania also controls who may do this work. The Department of Labor and Industry certifies lead contractors and requires a certified supervisor behind each firm, so one of the first questions to ask anyone is which credential fits your job.

Common questions

How do I know if I need lead abatement or just testing?

If you do not yet know whether the paint contains lead, start with testing. Abatement comes after an assessment finds a hazard. The guide on abatement vs lead-safe renovation matches common situations to services.

Does my Philadelphia house have lead paint?

If it was built before 1978, it might. Much of Philadelphia's housing predates the 1978 ban, and the older the house, the more likely lead paint is. Testing is the only way to know which surfaces carry it.

Is lead abatement different from a renovation?

Yes. Abatement is done to permanently eliminate lead hazards. Renovation disturbs paint as a side effect and needs lead-safe work practices.

Who can test for lead in Pennsylvania?

Pennsylvania certifies lead inspectors, risk assessors and abatement contractors through the Department of Labor and Industry, so ask which credential applies to your job before you schedule.

Lead Paint Testing and Inspection for Philadelphia Homes

Is that peeling paint actually lead? Color, texture and the age of a house cannot answer that question. A lead-based paint inspection identifies lead paint and its location. It is the right starting point when your main question is what materials you are about to disturb.

Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}

Request a call

Describe what you are seeing in the house and we will follow up. Prefer to talk? Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}.

For service inquiries only. If someone is in immediate danger or you suspect acute poisoning, call 911 or Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222.

What testing can tell you

An inspector may use an XRF instrument or laboratory analysis of paint samples. Ask which surfaces will be tested and whether the written report identifies components by room. A quick consumer swab is not a substitute for a documented professional inspection when a regulated report is needed.

Inspection or risk assessment?

An inspection locates lead paint. A risk assessment looks for current hazards and recommends controls. EPA explains why these are different services. If paint chips, window dust or bare soil are the concern, describe those conditions rather than requesting a paint test alone.

Prepare for the visit

Gather the construction date, any previous lead reports and a list of planned work. Mention doors, stair rails, porch surfaces and original window sashes. Testing should happen before sanding, scraping or demolition changes the condition of those surfaces.

Common questions

Who can perform a lead paint inspection in Pennsylvania?

Pennsylvania certifies lead occupations through the Department of Labor and Industry. Ask for the credential that matches the task before you schedule.

Is a general home inspection the same as a lead inspection?

No. A general home inspection does not identify lead paint surface by surface. A lead-based paint inspection uses XRF or laboratory analysis and produces a room-by-room record.

Do I need testing before a small remodel?

If the house predates 1978 and the work disturbs paint, identify the coatings first. Testing should happen before sanding, scraping or demolition changes the condition of those surfaces.

Lead Risk Assessment for Philadelphia Homes and Rentals

Dust keeps returning to the window sill. Paint is flaking near a toddler's play area. A risk assessment starts with the condition of the home and the ways someone could encounter lead, then turns findings into a plan.

Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}

Request a call

Describe what you are seeing in the house and we will follow up. Prefer to talk? Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}.

For service inquiries only. If someone is in immediate danger or you suspect acute poisoning, call 911 or Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222.

A report that connects the dots

A certified risk assessor evaluates deteriorated paint and may collect dust or soil samples. The report should describe hazards, their locations and options for dealing with them. Tell the assessor about recent renovations, accessible exterior soil and rooms used by children.

Choose the right professional

Pennsylvania certifies lead occupations through the Department of Labor and Industry, and the credential for an inspector, a risk assessor and an abatement firm are not the same. Verify current certification for the particular task. An EPA renovation certificate is not interchangeable with Pennsylvania abatement or risk-assessment qualifications.

A health result is not a building diagnosis

If a child has an elevated blood lead result, follow the healthcare provider's advice and contact the local health department. A home assessment can investigate environmental sources, but this website cannot diagnose exposure or determine medical treatment. Do not assume paint is the only possible source.

Common questions

Who can perform a lead risk assessment in Pennsylvania?

Pennsylvania distinguishes inspectors, risk assessors and abatement firms, and each task has its own certification through the Department of Labor and Industry. Verify the current certification for the specific work before you hire.

What does the report give me?

The report describes the hazards found, their locations and the options for controlling them, so the work that follows targets documented conditions rather than guesses.

A child's test came back high. Is this the right step?

Follow the healthcare provider's advice and contact the local health department first. A home assessment can investigate environmental sources, but it cannot diagnose exposure or replace medical guidance.

Lead Dust and Soil Hazard Control for Philadelphia Homes

The room may look clean while fine lead dust remains on floors and window troughs. Outside, deteriorating coatings can contaminate nearby soil. Professional sampling helps separate a visible mess from a measured hazard.

Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}

Request a call

Describe what you are seeing in the house and we will follow up. Prefer to talk? Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}.

For service inquiries only. If someone is in immediate danger or you suspect acute poisoning, call 911 or Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222.

Dust is not ordinary household dirt

Describe when dust appeared, whether work disturbed painted surfaces and which rooms or entry routes are affected. A professional plan may include specialized HEPA cleaning and wet-cleaning methods. Do not use a household vacuum as a substitute for a lead cleanup plan.

A bare patch outside can need assessment

Ask a risk assessor whether soil sampling is warranted around the drip line, a play area or other accessible ground. Paint chips in the soil do not establish the laboratory concentration. The control method depends on findings and site conditions, not a photograph of the yard.

Verify the outcome

EPA distinguishes paint, dust and soil hazards in risk assessments. When clearance is required, appearance alone does not establish a pass. Ask who samples, which laboratory analyzes the samples and what documentation you will receive.

Common questions

Can I just vacuum up the dust?

A household vacuum is not a substitute for a lead cleanup plan. Professional plans use specialized HEPA and wet-cleaning methods.

How do I know if my yard soil has lead?

Only sampling establishes the concentration. Ask a risk assessor whether soil sampling is warranted around the drip line, play areas or other accessible ground.

When is clearance required?

It depends on the project and the requirement behind the work. Ask who samples, which laboratory analyzes the samples and what documentation you will receive.

Lead Paint Removal and Abatement in Philadelphia, PA

Removing lead paint is not a normal repainting job. The work can create contaminated dust if it is done without the right controls. Start with the inspection or risk-assessment report so the abatement scope targets documented hazards.

Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}

Request a call

Describe what you are seeing in the house and we will follow up. Prefer to talk? Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}.

For service inquiries only. If someone is in immediate danger or you suspect acute poisoning, call 911 or Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222.

Removal is one option, not the only option

EPA describes abatement as permanent hazard elimination. Depending on the surface and its condition, a plan may use component replacement, enclosure, approved encapsulation or removal. Compare these choices with a qualified professional rather than assuming every painted surface must be stripped.

What belongs in the scope

Ask for the surfaces and rooms included, the containment plan, how occupants will be protected, cleanup procedures and the clearance arrangements. Discuss whether people or pets must leave the work area and who handles contaminated waste. Do not accept a verbal promise that ordinary painting will permanently solve a documented hazard.

Before work starts

Verify Pennsylvania credentials: the Department of Labor and Industry certifies lead abatement contractors and requires a certified supervisor behind each firm. Review any building permits or Philadelphia Historical Commission approvals separately. Avoid dry sanding or scraping suspect paint yourself while waiting. A price depends on the findings, access and chosen method, not a flat cost per house.

Common questions

Does every lead-painted surface have to be stripped?

No. Depending on the surface and its condition, a plan may use component replacement, enclosure, approved encapsulation or removal. Compare the options before assuming everything comes off.

Can I scrape the paint myself while I wait?

EPA advises against removing lead-based paint yourself. Avoid dry sanding or scraping suspect paint, and use trained, certified people for work that disturbs it.

What should a written abatement scope include?

The surfaces and rooms included, the containment plan, occupant protection, cleanup procedures and the clearance arrangements, plus who handles contaminated waste.

What happens to the paint behind the barrier?

Lead Abatement vs Lead-Safe Renovation

The same wall or window may be involved in very different projects. The purpose of the work helps determine which lead program applies.

Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}

Request a call

For service inquiries only. If someone is in immediate danger or you suspect acute poisoning, call 911 or Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222.

Abatement permanently addresses a hazard

EPA defines abatement as activity designed to permanently eliminate lead-based paint hazards. Pennsylvania certifies lead abatement contractors through the Department of Labor and Industry. Verify the firm and the individual qualifications for inspection, risk assessment or abatement.

Renovation changes the building

EPA's Renovation, Repair and Painting program covers paid work that disturbs paint in applicable older housing and child-occupied facilities. A kitchen remodel or replacement window project is not automatically abatement just because lead-safe practices are necessary.

Put the distinction in the proposal

Ask the professional to name the project type, certifications, methods and final documents. An RRP certificate alone is not proof of abatement qualifications. For a commercial-only building, other worker-safety rules may apply even where a residential lead rule does not.

Common questions

Is an RRP-certified renovation firm an abatement contractor?

Not automatically. An EPA renovation certificate is not interchangeable with Pennsylvania abatement or risk-assessment certifications. Verify the credential for the actual task.

Which one should I ask for?

Fishtown: rowhouse living and the dust old windows make

Fishtown's rowhouse blocks were built for workers who walked to the mills and factories nearby. Those houses have been painted and repainted for over a century, and the windows that stick and rub are often where a lead question starts.

Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}

Request a call

Describe what you are seeing in the house and we will follow up. Prefer to talk? Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}.

For service inquiries only. If someone is in immediate danger or you suspect acute poisoning, call 911 or Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222.

Rowhouses share their age, not their condition

The Encyclopedia of Greater Philadelphia describes Fishtown among the industrial neighborhoods whose row house blocks housed factory workers. That shared history makes lead paint a fair assumption to check, but only a test answers it for a specific house. Your neighbor's report is not your report.

Name the dust before naming the fix

Where does it collect: the sill, the trough, the floor under the window? Does it return within days of cleaning? Those observations tell a professional whether the question is a rubbing sash, a failing exterior coating or both. Describe the pattern instead of ordering a repaint.

Window work has more than one version

Repair with lead-safe practices, component replacement, enclosure and abatement are different projects with different documentation. Ask the firm to name the project type and its qualifications. A replacement sales pitch should not decide the hazard-control method.

Do not make dust while investigating

Avoid sanding or dry scraping suspect paint to see what is underneath. EPA's renovation guidance explains why paid paint disturbance in applicable older housing requires lead-safe practices. Keep children away from flaking areas until a professional has looked.

A useful first request

Send the approximate construction date, which windows or rooms are involved, photos of the damage and any earlier lead report. Ask what evaluation comes first and what documentation will show the work is done. A rowhouse block can look uniform from the street; the scope should still be written for your house.

Common questions

Do rowhouse neighbors share lead reports?

No. Rowhouses share their age, not their condition. Only a test answers the question for a specific house, so your neighbor's report is not yours.

What is friction dust?

Fine dust created when painted parts rub, like a sash moving in its frame. It can collect in window troughs and on sills without dramatic peeling paint.

Germantown: lead paint planning in one of America's oldest neighborhoods

Germantown has been building and rebuilding since 1683. Its houses carry original trim, wavy glass, deep porches and layers of paint from three centuries. Planning lead work here means protecting the details that make the neighborhood itself.

A historic name is not a diagnosis

The Encyclopedia of Greater Philadelphia calls Germantown one of America's most historic neighborhoods, with sites documented by the Historic American Buildings Survey. That context justifies checking painted components early. It does not prove that any particular surface contains lead. Testing does that.

List the components before choosing methods

Sash, frame, porch rail, exterior trim, interior doors: write down what the project will actually touch. A report that maps findings to that list keeps the scope honest. Different components on the same house can need different solutions.

Preservation approval is its own track

For a designated historic property, exterior changes may need Philadelphia Historical Commission review before components are ordered or removed. A lead plan does not grant preservation approval, and an approval does not address lead. Run both tracks in the same written scope so they do not collide mid-job.

Compare methods honestly

EPA identifies removal, special sealing and enclosure among abatement methods. Ordinary repainting is not permanent abatement, and a coating cannot fix unrelated dust or soil hazards. Ask what the chosen method leaves behind and what later maintenance must avoid.

Keep the record for the next owner

File the inspection, the scope, photos of existing conditions and the final documentation together. Do not call a house lead-free on the strength of a neat finish. Ask precisely what the evidence establishes and keep it where the next project can find it.

Common questions

Does historic designation change lead work?

It adds a separate approval track. For a designated property, discuss exterior changes with the Philadelphia Historical Commission before components are ordered or removed. A lead plan does not grant preservation approval.

Is encapsulation allowed on historic trim?

Suitability depends on the surface and the project. Ask what the method leaves behind and what later maintenance or renovation must avoid.

Chestnut Hill: renovating a big old house without a lead surprise

Chestnut Hill's large stone and frame houses grew with the railroad in the 1800s, and many are being renovated again. The safest remodel in a house that old starts by learning which painted surfaces the project will disturb.

The railroad built the Hill's housing

The Encyclopedia of Greater Philadelphia traces northwest Philadelphia's growth, including the 1854 railroad that connected Chestnut Hill to the city. The houses that followed have been updated many times, and each update can hide original painted components under newer finishes.

Sequence testing before demolition

Walls open fast in a remodel, and painted layers come apart faster. Test the surfaces the project will touch before sanding, scraping or demolition changes their condition. Bring the construction date, earlier reports and the project list to the inspection.

Renovation and abatement are different projects

EPA's renovation rule covers paid work that disturbs paint in applicable older housing; abatement permanently eliminates documented hazards. A kitchen remodel is not automatically abatement. Ask which project yours is and which credentials it needs.

Gardens and soil deserve a question too

Decades of exterior paint can flake toward the drip line. If bare soil sits near play areas or garden beds, ask a risk assessor whether soil sampling makes sense. Paint chips in the yard do not establish the laboratory concentration.

What a good scope looks like

Surfaces and rooms named, containment described, occupant protection arranged, cleanup specified and a final check agreed in advance. Keep it all in writing with the reports. A smooth finish is not proof the dust question was answered.

Common questions

When in a remodel should testing happen?

Before demolition. Bring the construction date, earlier reports and the project list to the inspection so the report maps to the components the work will disturb.

Is my renovation automatically abatement?

No. A remodel that disturbs paint needs lead-safe practices; abatement permanently eliminates documented hazards. The proposal should say which project it is.

Center City: lead planning for a business district in transition

Center City's office towers and older commercial blocks keep changing hands and uses. When a conversion or renovation disturbs old paint, lead planning belongs in the early discussion, before anyone assumes commercial and residential rules are the same.

Request a call

For service inquiries only. If someone is in immediate danger or you suspect acute poisoning, call 911 or Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222.

Conversions change the questions

The Encyclopedia of Greater Philadelphia documents Center City's long reinvention, from Market Street's commercial corridor to postwar urban renewal. Converting an office floor to housing is a different lead problem from repainting an office suite. Document present use, proposed use, building age and the surfaces the work will disturb.

Commercial-only is not automatically target housing

The EPA renovation rule focuses on applicable pre-1978 housing and child-occupied facilities. Do not apply that residential framework blindly to every storefront, and do not treat a commercial classification as permission to expose workers to lead dust. Ask the project's safety professionals which worker-protection and waste rules apply.

Separate the investigations

Paint testing, asbestos surveys, structural review and other environmental checks answer different questions. A lead report does not clear other materials. For mixed-use projects, the scope should say which spaces and components were evaluated and which were not.

Plan access and occupancy

A multi-floor project may have occupied suites, shared lobbies and staged work. Describe those conditions to the professional writing the control plan. Ask how occupants and later contractors stay out of affected areas, and avoid reopening promises until findings and approvals are known.

A request that gets a useful answer

Provide intended use, floor count, construction history, drawings and any existing reports. State whether you need evaluation, permanent hazard control or renovation safety planning. No contractor can guarantee a permitting or licensing outcome, so treat such promises as a warning sign.

Common questions

Do residential lead rules apply to an office conversion?

The EPA renovation rule focuses on applicable pre-1978 housing and child-occupied facilities. A conversion to housing changes that analysis, so document the present and proposed use and ask which framework applies.

What should a conversion lead request include?

The intended use, floor count, construction history, drawings and any existing reports, plus whether you need evaluation, permanent hazard control or renovation safety planning.
